## Introduction

Clear, compelling framing of the phenomenon, research question, and why it matters; variables and context are intelligible.

## Methods
```{r} 
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)
library(psych)
library(performance)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(lmtest)
library(emmeans)
library(ggeffects)
library(sandwich)
library(patchwork)

# Loading dataset
my_data <- read.xlsx("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agraha89/graham-capstone/main/Dataset.xlsx", sheet = 1)

#### Scoring Scales ####
moderation_analysis.df <- my_data
v_keys <- list(
  Sexual_Objectification_Experiences = c("SO1", "SO2", "SO3", "SO4", "SO5", "SO6", "SO7", "SO8", "SO9", "SO10", "SO11"),
  Benevolent_Sexism = c("BS1", "BS2", "BS3", "BS4", "BS5", "BS6"),
  Safety_Anxiety = c("PSA1", "PSA2", "PSA3", "PSA4", "PSA5", "PSA6", "PSA7", "PSA8")) 

# Scoring Sexual Objectification Experiences Scale
SO_scores <- scoreItems(
  v_keys["Sexual_Objectification_Experiences"],
  moderation_analysis.df,
  totals = F,
  min = 1,
  max = 5,
  impute = "mean") # Using mean imputation to handle missing item values

# Scoring Benevolent Sexism Subscale
BS_scores <- scoreItems(
  v_keys["Benevolent_Sexism"],
  moderation_analysis.df,
  totals = F,
  min = 1,
  max = 5,
  impute = "mean")

# Scoring Personal Safety Anxiety Scale
PSA_scores <- scoreItems(
  v_keys["Safety_Anxiety"],
  moderation_analysis.df,
  totals = F,
  min = 1,
  max = 7,
  impute = "mean")

# Creating and combining dataframes of scores
SO_scores.df <- as.data.frame(SO_scores$scores)
BS_scores.df <- as.data.frame(BS_scores$scores)
PSA_scores.df <- as.data.frame(PSA_scores$scores)
allscores.df <- cbind(SO_scores.df, BS_scores.df, PSA_scores.df) |> 
  mutate(SO_c = Sexual_Objectification_Experiences - mean(Sexual_Objectification_Experiences),
         BS_c = Benevolent_Sexism - mean(Benevolent_Sexism),
         SA_c = Safety_Anxiety - mean(Safety_Anxiety))  # Centred AFTER dropping missing cases
```
Lucid account of data source, sample, variables, preparation, models, comparisons, diagnostics, and rationale for major decisions; sufficient detail without a code walkthrough

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8
((SO_by_BS_plot + SO_by_PSA_plot) / BS_by_PSA_plot) +
    plot_annotation(title = "Scatterplots for Key Measures",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 20)))

## Intercept-only Model
mod0 <- lm(SA_c ~ 1, data = allscores.df)

# Single-predictor model
mod1 <- lm(SA_c ~ SO_c, data = allscores.df)

# Two-predictor model
mod2 <- lm(SA_c ~ SO_c + BS_c, data = allscores.df)

# Interaction model
mod3 <- lm(SA_c ~ SO_c + BS_c + SO_c * BS_c, data = allscores.df)

# Running nested model comparisons
tests <- anova(mod0, mod1, mod2, mod3)

nested.f.tests <- tests |>
  select(Res.Df, Df, F, `Pr(>F)`) |> # Selecting relevant stats to keep
  rename("Residual DF" = Res.Df,
         "Change in Df" = Df,
         "Nested F" = F,
         "Nested p" = `Pr(>F)`) |> 
  mutate(`Nested p` = ifelse(`Nested p` < 0.001,
                             "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", `Nested p`))) |> 
  mutate(Model = c("Intercept-only", "M1: SO Experiences", "M2: + Benevolent Sexism", "M3: + Interaction")) |> # Adding informative model labels
  relocate(Model, .before = 1)

# Extracting overall model performance
glance0 <- glance(mod0)
glance1 <- glance(mod1)
glance2 <- glance(mod2)
glance3 <- glance(mod3)

# Combining individual model performance metrics into one dataframe
glances <- rbind(glance0,
                 glance1,
                 glance2,
                 glance3) |> 
  mutate(Model = c("Intercept-only", "M1: SO Experiences", "M2: + Benevolent Sexism", "M3: + Interaction")) |> 
  relocate(Model, .before = 1)

# Creating gt table
nested.f.tests.table <- gt(nested.f.tests) |> 
  fmt_number(columns = c("Nested F"), decimals = 2) |> 
  cols_align(align = "left")

## Combining nested tests and model performance
comparison_table <- cbind(
  Model = glances,
  nested.f.tests)

# Selecting relevants statistics for table
comparison_table <- comparison_table |>
  mutate(Delta.R2 = Model.r.squared - lag(Model.r.squared),
         RMSE = c(sqrt(mean(residuals(mod0)^2)),
                  sqrt(mean(residuals(mod1)^2)),
                  sqrt(mean(residuals(mod2)^2)),
                  sqrt(mean(residuals(mod3)^2)))) |>
  select(Model.Model,
         Model.r.squared,
         Delta.R2,
         Model.adj.r.squared,
         RMSE,
         "Residual DF",
         Model.df,
         "Nested F",
         "Nested p",
         Model.AIC)

## Displaying combined model-comparison table
comparison_table |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(
    Model.r.squared,
    Model.adj.r.squared,
    RMSE,
    Delta.R2,
    "Nested F"),
    decimals = 2) |>
  sub_missing(columns = c(Delta.R2, Model.df, "Nested F", "Nested p"),
              missing_text = "—") |> 
  cols_label(Model.Model = "Model",
             Model.r.squared = "R²",
             Model.adj.r.squared = "Adjusted R²",
             RMSE = "RMSE",
             Delta.R2 = "ΔR²",
             "Residual DF" = "Residual df",
             Model.df = "Nested df") |> 
  cols_move(columns = Delta.R2,
            after = "Residual DF") |> 
  tab_header(title = "Nested Model Comparisons")

# Evaluate Regression Diagnostics
#plot(mod3) plots suggest that observations 11, 20, 33, 83, and 209 may bias the regression analysis

plot(check_model(mod3)) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Diagnostic Plots for Model 3")

## Plots suggest no influential observations, but slight curvature at tail ends of normality of residuals plot and at left tail of homogeneity of variance plot
# Although observations 11, 33, and 309 were flagged in the earlier diagnostic plot, all observations sit within the contour lines here
```

# Modelling standardized residuals to see what proportion have sample/theoretical quantiles +/- 2SDs
std_res <- rstandard(mod3)

percent_above_2_quantiles <- mean(abs(std_res) > 2) * 100 # 4.9% --> Within normal, so residual normality is not a concern here

#### Model 3 with HC3 Estimator
HC3 is a heteroscedasticity-consistent standard error estimator for linear regression that adjusts squared OLS residuals by leverage to keep hypothesis tests accurate when error variance is unequal. In essence, it will make more accurate predictions about variance by widening standard error estimates

```{r}
# Reporting regression results for original model with HC3 SE estimate
coefficient_results <- tidy(coeftest(mod3, vcov = vcovHC(mod3, type = "HC3")),
                                        conf.int = TRUE,
                                        conf.level = 0.95)

coefficient_results |>
  mutate(term = dplyr::recode(term,
                              "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
                              "SO_c" = "Sexual Objectification Experience Frequency",
                              "BS_c" = "Benevolent Sexism",
                              "SO_c:BS_c" = "Sexual Objectification × Benevolent Sexism")) |>
  select(term,
         estimate,
         std.error,
         conf.low,
         conf.high,
         p.value) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(term = "Predictor",
             estimate = "Estimate",
             std.error = "SE",
             conf.low = "95% CI lower",
             conf.high = "95% CI upper",
             p.value = "p") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(
    estimate,
    std.error,
    conf.low,
    conf.high),
    decimals = 3) |>
  fmt(columns = p.value,
      fns = function(x) {
        ifelse(
          x < .001,
          "< .001",
          sprintf("%.3f", x))}) |> 
  tab_header(title = "Interaction Model Results with HC3 Estimator")

# Simple slopes: Looking at influence of sexual objectification frequency at specific values of benevolent sexism
# Pick the probing values: low (-1 SD), average (mean) and high (+1 SD) benevolent sexism
BS_mean <- mean(allscores.df$BS_c, na.rm = TRUE)
BS_sd <- sd(allscores.df$BS_c, na.rm = TRUE)
BS_values <- BS_mean + c(-1, 0, 1) * BS_sd

# Simple slopes for sexual objectification frequency at each benevolent sexism value.
HC3_BS_trends <- emtrends(mod3,
                             specs = ~ BS_c,
                             var = "SO_c",
                             at = list(BS_c = BS_values),
                             vcov. = vcovHC(mod3, type = "HC3"))

# Building a data frame of the simple slopes
HC3_simple_slopes_df <- summary(HC3_BS_trends,
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE),
  null = 0) |> 
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(BS_level = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")) |>
  select(BS_level, SO_c.trend, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value, lower.CL, upper.CL)

## Turning the simple slopes dataframe into a table
HC3_simple_slopes_table <- gt(HC3_simple_slopes_df) |> 
  cols_label(BS_level = "Benevolent Sexism",
             SO_c.trend = "Estimate",
             lower.CL = "Lower 95% CI",
             upper.CL = "Upper 95% CI",
             t.ratio = "t",
             p.value = "p") |> 
fmt_number(columns = c(SO_c.trend, SE, t.ratio, lower.CL, upper.CL), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt(columns = p.value,
      fns = \(x) scales::pvalue(x, accuracy = 0.001, add_p = FALSE)) |>
  cols_move(columns = c(lower.CL, upper.CL),
    after = SE) |> 
  tab_header(title = "Simple Effects of Sexual Objectication Frequency Across Levels of Benevolent Sexism")

# Generating predicted outcomes to prepare visualization
HC3_predictions <- ggpredict(mod3,
  terms = c("SO_c", "BS_c [meansd]"), # Specifying the three levels of benevolent sexism
  vcov.fun = sandwich::vcovHC,
  vcov.type = "HC3")

# Un-centering the mean to make scale values more interpretable
predictions_df <- as.data.frame(HC3_predictions) |> 
  mutate(SO_original = x + m_SO,
    BS_original = as.numeric(as.character(group)) + m_BS,
    predicted_original = predicted + m_PSA,
    conf.low_original = conf.low + m_PSA,
    conf.high_original = conf.high + m_PSA)

# Creating plot
HC3_plot <- ggplot(predictions_df,
         aes(x = SO_original, y = predicted_original,
             colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low_original, ymax = conf.high_original),
    alpha = 0.15,
    colour = NA) +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Sexual Objectification Experience Frequency",
    y = "Predicted Safety Anxiety",
    colour = "Benevolent Sexism",
    fill = "Benevolent Sexism",
    title = "Simple Slopes of Objectification Frequency at Levels of Benevolent Sexism")

HC3_simple_slopes_table

HC3_plot
```
#### Sensitivity Model with HC3 Estimator
```{r}
# Sensitivity model without observations that were flagged by diagnostic tests
mod3_sensitivity <- lm(SA_c ~ SO_c * BS_c,
  data = allscores.df[-c(11, 20, 33, 83, 193, 209, 225), ])

# Reporting regression results for *sensitivity* model with HC3 SE estimate
sensitivity_coefficient_results <- tidy(coeftest(mod3_sensitivity, vcov = vcovHC(mod3_sensitivity, type = "HC3")),
                                        conf.int = TRUE,
                                        conf.level = 0.95)

sensitivity_coefficient_results |>
  mutate(term = dplyr::recode(term,
                              "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
                              "SO_c" = "Sexual Objectification Experience Frequency",
                              "BS_c" = "Benevolent Sexism",
                              "SO_c:BS_c" = "Sexual Objectification × Benevolent Sexism")) |>
  select(term,
         estimate,
         std.error,
         conf.low,
         conf.high,
         p.value) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(term = "Predictor",
             estimate = "Estimate",
             std.error = "SE",
             conf.low = "95% CI lower",
             conf.high = "95% CI upper",
             p.value = "p") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(
    estimate,
    std.error,
    conf.low,
    conf.high),
    decimals = 3) |>
  fmt(columns = p.value,
      fns = function(x) {
        ifelse(
          x < .001,
          "< .001",
          sprintf("%.3f", x))}) |> 
  tab_header(title = "Sensitivity Interaction Model Results with HC3 Estimator")

# Simple slopes for sensitivity model (also using HC3 estimates)
Sensitivity_BS_trends <- emtrends(mod3_sensitivity,
                          specs = ~ BS_c,
                          var = "SO_c",
                          at = list(BS_c = BS_values),
                          vcov. = vcovHC(mod3_sensitivity, type = "HC3"))

# Building a data frame of the simple slopes
Sensitivity_simple_slopes_df <- summary(Sensitivity_BS_trends,
                                infer = c(TRUE, TRUE),
                                null = 0) |> 
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(BS_level = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")) |>
  select(BS_level, SO_c.trend, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value, lower.CL, upper.CL)

## Turning the simple slopes dataframe into a table
Sensitivity_simple_slopes_table <- gt(Sensitivity_simple_slopes_df) |> 
  cols_label(BS_level = "Benevolent Sexism",
             SO_c.trend = "Estimate",
             lower.CL = "Lower 95% CI",
             upper.CL = "Upper 95% CI",
             t.ratio = "t",
             p.value = "p") |> 
  fmt_number(columns = c(SO_c.trend, SE, t.ratio, lower.CL, upper.CL), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt(columns = p.value,
      fns = \(x) scales::pvalue(x, accuracy = 0.001, add_p = FALSE)) |>
  cols_move(columns = c(lower.CL, upper.CL),
            after = SE) |> 
  tab_header(title = "Simple Effects of Sexual Objectication Frequency Across Levels of Benevolent Sexism")

# Generating predicted outcomes to prepare visualization
Sensitivity_predictions <- ggpredict(mod3_sensitivity,
                             terms = c("SO_c", "BS_c [meansd]"), # Specifying the three levels of benevolent sexism
                             vcov.fun = sandwich::vcovHC,
                             vcov.type = "HC3")

# Calculating means with observations removed
sensitivity_scores <- allscores.df[-c(11, 20, 33, 83, 193, 209, 225), ] |> 
  select(Sexual_Objectification_Experiences, Benevolent_Sexism, Safety_Anxiety) |> 
  describe()

sensitivity_m_SO <- round(sensitivity_scores$mean[1], 2)
sensitivity_m_BS <- round(sensitivity_scores$mean[2], 2) 
sensitivity_m_PSA <- round(sensitivity_scores$mean[3], 2)

# Un-centering the mean to make scale values more interpretable
Sensitivity_predictions_df <- as.data.frame(Sensitivity_predictions) |> 
  mutate(SO_original = x + sensitivity_m_SO,
         BS_original = as.numeric(as.character(group)) + sensitivity_m_BS,
         predicted_original = predicted + sensitivity_m_PSA,
         conf.low_original = conf.low + sensitivity_m_PSA,
         conf.high_original = conf.high + sensitivity_m_PSA)

# Creating plot
Sensitivity_plot <- ggplot(Sensitivity_predictions_df,
                   aes(x = SO_original, y = predicted_original,
                       colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low_original, ymax = conf.high_original),
              alpha = 0.15,
              colour = NA) +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Sexual Objectification Experience Frequency",
       y = "Predicted Safety Anxiety",
       colour = "Benevolent Sexism",
       fill = "Benevolent Sexism",
       title = "Simple Slopes of Objectification Frequency at Levels of Benevolent Sexism")

Sensitivity_simple_slopes_table
Sensitivity_plot
```
